clue.text: Youth, top one, last to be involved in tie-break? Not at Wimbledon

indicators.note: letters that become involved are mixed up together, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young player, the best of the side, is the final one dragged into a deciding contest that is not tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be involved' is the anagram signal working on YOUTH TOP ONE LAST. Tennis has its own tie-break, so the question mark and 'Not at Wimbledon' steer to football's version.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a drawn knockout match is settled by alternating spot kicks, the sport's equivalent of a tennis tie-break.

clue.text: Prudent, like extremely savvy Scottish smoker, securing permission to stay

parts.note: politic means shrewd and prudent
a la (French) means in the style of, like

indicators.note: extremely means take only the outermost letters of the word savvy

parts.note: lum is the Scots word for a chimney, which smokes

explanation.surface: A careful, canny Scot with a pipe is granted leave to remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish smoker' is not a pipe-smoking Scot but a chimney: LUM in Scots dialect. 'like' gives A LA, from the French à la.
explanation.definitionFit: Refugees fleeing persecution are granted this protection, which is formal leave to remain in a foreign country.

clue.text: One at first not into big bites, leaving expensive restaurant?

definitions.text: One at first not into big bites, leaving expensive restaurant?

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the seven words that follow

parts.words: not into big bites, leaving expensive restaurant

explanation.surface: A diner who takes little mouthfuls walks out of a pricey restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone not into big bites. 'One' stands outside the acrostic and only frames the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes small bites rather than big mouthfuls eats in little pecks, as a mouse at cheese.

clue.text: Truly less extreme gathering

parts.note: lite is marketing language for a milder, toned-down version
a rally is a mass gathering of people

explanation.surface: A genuinely moderate assembly of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are intensifiers meaning actually or really, as in 'it was truly enormous'.

clue.text: Scene of fighting — push not ending after year

indicators.note: after places the shortened push behind the year's letter
not ending means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: to press is to push

explanation.surface: A battle scene where the advance stalls after a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian town was the site of several major battles of the First World War.

clue.text: Realistic, moved fast to protect daughter and son after upset

indicators.note: to protect means the first piece surrounds and shields the others

parts.note: hared means ran quickly, like a hare

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word son is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: son is taken as written

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth parent rushed to shield the children after a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where reversing means reading from the bottom upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tough-minded and unsentimental is practical and realistic about how things are.

clue.text: East German I asked originally to identify old Rome's port

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of the word asked

explanation.surface: A man from East Germany asks where ancient Rome's harbour was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' is not a person from the old GDR but the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: This town at the Tiber's mouth served as the harbour city for ancient Rome.

clue.text: Instrument in auto, car in America

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A musical instrument travelling in a car across America.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, sometimes called a sweet potato.

clue.text: Unusual Web post there about Derby authorities?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the hat
unusual signals the letters of these words are put in an uncommon order

parts.note: a derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: An odd online message there concerning the Derby horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the race or the city but is a bowler hat, HAT, which the anagram of WEB POST THERE goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: This set phrase names the people or bodies in control, the establishment holding power.

clue.text: Aims high most of time, providing seafood

parts.note: to lob is to send a ball high in the air

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the time word is dropped

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone ambitious most of the time ends up feeding people fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large marine crustacean with claws, served as a luxury shellfish dish.

clue.text: Suspicion after artist in continual struggle

indicators.note: after places the suspicion word behind the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a trace or suspicion is a tiny hint of something

explanation.surface: A painter is suspected of being caught in a never-ending battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the exhausting competitive grind of modern working life.

clue.text: Worker in trial year regularly absent

indicators.note: regularly absent means every other letter of trial year goes missing, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: An employee on probation is often off sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays tiles on roofs, floors or walls is one kind of worker.

clue.text: Changed, a man irons in republic

indicators.note: changed means these letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A transformed man does the ironing in a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny independent state enclosed by Italy, one of the world's oldest republics.

clue.text: Singers and visitors welcoming returning soldiers

indicators.note: welcoming means the visitors take the soldiers in

parts.note: callers are people who visit

indicators.note: returning means the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Musicians and house guests greet soldiers coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: These seasonal performers go door to door at Christmas singing festive songs.

clue.text: National of Haiti? Nope, wrong

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters given are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person is from Haiti and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the East African country whose capital is Addis Ababa.

clue.text: Refrain from using duplicate

definitions.meaning: to hold back from using something, as in sparing the rod
a duplicate is an extra kept in reserve, like a second key

explanation.surface: Don't use the copy.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to do without or withhold; the other is a reserve copy held in case.

clue.text: Upright guy, Greek character, willing

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, any guy
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
on means willing, as in 'I'm on'

explanation.surface: An honest fellow, a Greek of good character, is ready and keen.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical post or pole used as a support, so an upright.

clue.text: Freshly starting, fast, with too much to say?

indicators.note: freshly starting means the word for fast gets a new first letter in place of its old one

parts.note: nippy means quick and fast

explanation.surface: Someone new to fasting complains a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly starting' gives the fast word a fresh start: its N is swapped for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheeky and answering back is British slang for having too much mouth.

clue.text: At work prepare for one who should improve wall's appearance

definitions.text: one who should improve wall's appearance

indicators.note: at work means the letters of prepare are set working into a new order

explanation.surface: On the job, a decorator gets ready to brighten up a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator who hangs wallpaper smartens up the walls of a room.

clue.text: Retreats from initially hostile notion habits will follow

indicators.note: will follow places the habits word after the notion
initially asks for the opening letter of the word hostile

parts.note: an idea is a notion
ways are habits or customs

explanation.surface: Withdrawals from an unfriendly concept, with routines trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden places to escape to are secluded refuges, the sense of retreats as nouns.

clue.text: Expert skill, going over area again

indicators.note: going over means the skill word covers the other letters

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
bis is Latin for twice, used to call for a repeat

explanation.surface: A skilled specialist revisits an area once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of the Arabic language and culture is a specialist in that field.

clue.text: Reserve restrains a flyer in game

indicators.note: restrains means the reserve holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
per means a, as in so much per head
an owl is a bird, a flyer

explanation.surface: A substitute holds back a bird during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual championship match of American football, the NFL's final.

clue.text: Avril keenly embracing poet

indicators.note: embracing means these words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Avril hugs a poet with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was the Austrian lyric poet of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Something used by cowboy's girl — ring

parts.note: a lass is a girl
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A cowboy's girlfriend gets a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'cowboy's' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose that a cowhand throws to catch cattle.

clue.text: Vehicle instructor

explanation.surface: A driving teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a bus or horse-drawn carriage; the other is a trainer who teaches.

clue.text: Folklore leitmotif? To some extent perhaps she is

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether a recurring figure of folklore might be a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine siren of German legend is herself a recurring theme of folklore.

clue.text: Satirical piece about uncompleted bio that boosts you on holiday?

indicators.note: about means the sketch goes round the shortened word

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch

indicators.note: uncompleted means the biography word loses its final letter

parts.note: a life is a biography

explanation.surface: A satirical sketch about an unfinished biography cheers you up on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosts' looks like a mood lift; it is a literal one, up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable-hauled chair or tow carries skiers uphill at a winter resort.

clue.text: Queen Mum right: that's a new weighty piece, covering one better missed outside

parts.note: ma is mum, mother
i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: covering means the weight word wraps round the one

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: missed outside means the word better loses its outermost letters

explanation.surface: The Queen Mother is right that a new heavy item covers one punter who failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed outside' strips B and R from BETTER, leaving ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The last queen of France before the Revolution, wife of Louis XVI, guillotined in 1793.
